status: Side-view motion pilot, not production atlas
prompts:
Create one six-frame side-view walk-cycle sprite strip, EXACTLY SIX columns and ONE row, for the SAME headless compact chibi male game body from reference image 2. Reference 1 is the motion authority: six consecutive sampled phases of a real complete two-step walking cycle facing SCREEN RIGHT. Reference 2 provides ONLY the costume, painterly rendering style and compact torso/short leg proportions, NEVER its broken poses. Turquoise long sleeve sweatshirt, orange crossbody pouch, cream cargo trousers, orange sneakers, bare neck stump; NO head and no cape. Transparent background. Six equally sized cells, identical neck anchor, body scale and floor baseline. Each sprite large and clear within its own cell, ample separation. No text, border or motion marks.

Transfer the motion from photo columns 1 through 6 respectively. Keep anatomical identity across frames: the NEAR arm and NEAR leg are one side of the body, FAR arm and FAR leg are the opposite side. Near limbs rendered in front, far limbs partially hidden by torso/near limbs. The NEAR leg is trailing in pose 1, passing forward in pose 2, reaching forward in pose 3; then leading/supporting in pose 4, supporting while FAR leg passes in pose 5, trailing in pose 6. The NEAR arm swings forward in pose 1, near vertical in pose 2, backward in pose 3, backward in pose 4, near vertical in pose 5, forward in pose 6. FAR arm always opposite NEAR arm. Observe photography occlusion. Do not substitute the same leg for both half cycles. Contact/passing/advance then opposite contact/passing/advance. Both legs must overlap at the passing phases. Legs must not remain spread in all frames.

Adapt arms to user's straight-arm walk: each shoulder-elbow-wrist forms one nearly straight line at every phase (elbow 175-180 degrees), natural pendulum swing from shoulder. No hand on chest/pouch, no raised forearms, no fists at waist. Both hands relaxed below hip level except slight swing height changes. Small arm swing, no exaggerated march. Preserve compact proportions from costume reference, but articulation must follow the photographic motion. One consistent costume across all six frames. This is an isolated six-frame motion sample, not a full four-direction atlas.

Edit this six-column one-row headless character sprite strip. Keep costume, scale, anchors, transparent background and six cell positions. Correct gait anatomically using a FIXED NEAR side (camera-facing side, limbs visibly layered ON TOP of torso/other leg) and FAR side (occluded behind). Crucial: clothing cargo pocket belongs to the NEAR thigh and moves WITH that thigh, not arbitrarily between legs. NEAR sleeve attaches visible foreground shoulder and stays same anatomical arm. Arms straight, no bent elbows. All sprites face RIGHT.

Frame1 keep: NEAR thigh and shoe forward/right, FAR leg back/left; NEAR hand BACK/LEFT of hip, FAR hand forward/right. 
Frame2 keep the near leg supporting directly beneath hip, far leg lifting through.
Frame3 CHANGE: NEAR leg extended BACK/LEFT, its cargo pocket visibly on the backward near thigh; FAR leg extended FORWARD/RIGHT behind it. NEAR arm extended FORWARD/RIGHT (foreground sleeve crossing in front of torso at hip height), FAR arm back/left partly hidden. Near elbow straight, not a curled bicep.
Frame4 CHANGE: same anatomical arrangement as frame3 but opposite contact phase: FAR heel leads on RIGHT and NEAR toe trails on LEFT. NEAR hand forward/right, FAR hand back/left. Its pose must be the anatomical opposite of frame1.
Frame5 CHANGE: FAR leg vertical supporting beneath hip behind; NEAR knee bent and moving forward through vertical, NEAR foot lifted. Near/far arms almost vertical, near arm foreground.
Frame6 CHANGE: NEAR leg reaches FORWARD/RIGHT, FAR leg back/left. NEAR straight arm swings BACK/LEFT of hip in foreground; FAR arm swings forward/right behind torso. This prepares frame1 contact.

Use the exact limb assignments above; do not put the large visible foreground sleeve backward in frames3/4 or forward in frame6. Reconstruct overlapping shapes properly, exactly two arms and two legs each, no disembodied hands. Same short stocky game-body proportions. No labels.
